subject: Interpretation of coeffiecients between binary exogenous and endogenous variables estimated with WLSMV

messages.author: d810b9504a291a31
messages.subject: Interpretation of coeffiecients between binary exogenous and endogenous variables estimated with WLSMV
parts:
Dear all,

I try to understand how I have to interpret the coeffiecients calculated in my full SEM with a binary dependent endogenous variable. I calculated the Model in R with the package Lavaan and used the WLSMV estimator - DWLS was used to estimate the model parameters, but the full weight matrix to compute robust standard errors, and a mean- and variance-adjusted test statistic. Now, I am not sure whether I can interpret the coefficients like in a linear probability regression.
For exampel one regression coeffient estimated in my model is between gender (0=male, 1=female) and having a fixed term employment contract (0 permanent contract, 1=fixed-term contract) and has the value 0.146. Interpreted as a linear regression coeffient it would mean that women have a 14.6 percentage points higher probabilty to have a fixed-term contract than men.
Is this interpreation right for the coefficient estimated with the WLSMV estimator or do I have to interpret it in a different way?

Thank you  a lot in advance.

Best regards
Leona

messages.author: bec3b6c763e426c0
messages.subject: Re: Interpretation of coeffiecients between binary exogenous and endogenous variables estimated with WLSMV
parts:
In robust WLS estimation (e.g., WLSMV), and focusing on the standardized solution, the beta coefficients estimate the amount of standard deviation change in the latent response variable (LRV) for each one standard deviation  increase  in the predictor. This interpretation is the same whether you applied delta or theta parameterization.
If you want to focus on the unstandardized solution:
  • Delta parameterization (total variance of LRV fixed to 1): coefficients estimate the amount of unit change in the LRV for each one unit  increase  in the predictor.
  • Theta parameterization (residual variance of LRV fixed to 1):  coefficients estimate the amount of change in probit (normal deviate) units in the LRV for each one unit increase in the predictor.
Source: Kline (2016, Ch. 13)
